profile.campus: Aurora, Arapahoe County, Colorado (QTS Aurora-Denver 1 campus)
profile.address: 1160 N Gun Club Rd, Aurora, CO 80018
profile.reading:
QTS's own site places this data center at 1160 N Gun Club Rd in Aurora, Colorado, inside Arapahoe County, on a 65-acre campus that the company owns outright. QTS markets the site as planned for 160 megawatts or more of critical power capacity, phrasing this registry reads as a build-out target for the fully developed campus rather than a confirmed operating figure for what stands today. QTS does not publish a per-building square footage or a cooling-redundancy rating for the property. The company's own marketing copy for Aurora-Denver 1 references its in-house "Freedom Standard Design" building approach and describes the 65-acre parcel as offering substantial room for future expansion, though no specific construction-phase timeline or current building count is disclosed.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, by Chad Williams, and it grew through a mix of acquisitions and ground-up construction into a national wholesale and colocation platform. The company went public in 2013 as QTS Realty Trust, a real estate investment trust that traded on the New York Stock Exchange. That public chapter ended when Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust led a take-private acquisition valued at roughly $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021, according to Blackstone's own press release. QTS has not been an independent SEC filer since, which limits how much financial and operational detail about individual sites like Aurora-Denver 1 is now disclosed compared with the company's REIT-era filings.

QTS describes itself as a hyperscale-neutral wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model closer to peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne than to a company like Amazon Web Services. Since the Blackstone deal closed in August 2021, QTS has kept expanding rather than pulling back, with publicly documented projects that include a 750 megawatt, 375-acre campus near Phoenix acquired for $255.3 million in July 2022 and two large campuses in the Dallas-Fort Worth area at Irving and Fort Worth, a pace of growth broadly consistent with QTS activity this registry has also documented in Northern Virginia, Georgia, and Ohio.

QTS's current portfolio language on its own site describes more than 30 facilities across North America and Europe, without breaking that figure down state by state. No independently sourced, per-building capacity or square-footage number specific to the Aurora-Denver 1 building has turned up in this research beyond the planned campus-wide power figure described above. Readers should treat the 160 megawatt-plus figure as QTS's own stated ambition for the site rather than a verified, present-day operating capacity.

sources.title: Blackstone Funds Complete Acquisition of QTS Realty Trust

reading.body:
QTS Aurora-Denver 1 sits on a 65-acre campus in Arapahoe County that QTS owns outright and markets as planned for 160 megawatts or more of critical power capacity. QTS describes this as a build-out target for the fully developed campus rather than a confirmed operating figure for what stands today. No per-building square footage, current operating capacity, cooling redundancy rating, construction timeline, or building count is published.

At the assumed density of 40 kilowatts per rack for AI training workloads, 160 megawatts of IT load would support roughly 4,000 racks. The campus has room for substantial future expansion, and QTS operates as a wholesale colocation landlord leasing to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than running its own end-user services. Since its August 2021 acquisition by Blackstone, QTS has expanded rather than contracted, with documented large projects in Phoenix and the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

Within Colorado, 17 data center facilities are mapped and three publish power figures totaling 26.35 megawatts. Aurora-Denver 1 would rank fourth by published megawatts in the state if its 160 megawatt figure were operating today rather than a planned capacity. No independent verification of current operating power at this campus has been published.
